First, we express $f(x)$ as a composite function:

$$
f={e}^{g},\,g=\operatorname{tanh}⁡s,\,s={x}^{2}
$$

The chain rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}s}\cdot \frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}={e}^{g},\,\frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}s}={sech}^{2}⁡s,\,\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}x}=2x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, multiplying the three results together and substituting for $g$ and $s$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & ={e}^{g}\cdot {sech}^{2}⁡s\cdot 2x \\  & ={e}^{\operatorname{tanh}⁡{x}^{2}}\cdot {sech}^{2}⁡{x}^{2}\cdot 2x \\  & =2x{e}^{\operatorname{tanh}⁡{x}^{2}}{sech}^{2}⁡{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
